text:
Here is the result of "fetch" for the Page with URL https://app.notion.com/p/3cfe245ae5f3815ab5b6cf00e712f8ff as of 2026-09-02T22:38:25.900Z: {"title":"Stephen Hammond · Council · inc"} {"type":"emoji","emoji":"🧩"} **Filled card. Not published.** Stephen Hammond · Council · incumbent (2022–26 City term). Scored 2 Sep 2026 against **The Program — A City That Works v1.10 (31 Jul 2026)** using the 12-topic template and Decision 14. **The letter on this card is a dash.** An internal proposal sits at the bottom of the page and is Joa's to apply or reject. Alignment compute APPLIED letter for Hammond stays **—**. Do not stamp 35.52 as an ACTW figure. **Revision 2 · 2 Sep 2026 (second pass).** Arithmetic corrected (the first pass summed 10 marks to 12.5; the true sum of those marks was 11.5). Two cells re-marked upward on sources the first pass did not carry: row 21 and row 52. One cell added as 📋 Record: row 31. Five cells re-sourced onto non-paywalled URLs. Full change list in the working notes. ## Card
Field Value
Name Stephen Hammond
Office Council
Kind inc (2022–26 City term — Record in the cell; sourced miss caps below Close; non-contradicting Record = 📋 not in n)
Platform URL (2026) [https://www.votestephenhammond.ca/priorities](https://www.votestephenhammond.ca/priorities)
Platform lastmod Not published. No lastmod tag, no copyright year, no dated posts on the platform pages; /sitemap.xml returns 404. Newest dated item anywhere on the site is the 10 Apr 2026 op-ed listed on /news, under a "Campaign Updates — Coming Soon" placeholder. Site is authorized (financial agent named in the footer). Record lines 📋 (shown, not scored) **7** — Missing Middle NO 26 Jan 2023 (row 1) · VicPD call-data FOI published Aug 2023 (row 9) · daytime-sheltering YES, he moved it, 18 Jul 2024 (row 10) · budget NO 7 May 2026 (row 13) · security cost-spreading motion, he moved it, defeated 6 Jul 2023 (row 31) · officer-cut NO 3 Mar 2026 (row 33) · amalgamation-question NO 25 Jun 2026 (row 55). All matching, none in n.
Letter (only at 5 scored answers: B+, B, C, D, or —) **—** · awaiting Joa's click. Internal proposal at the bottom of this page. Alignment compute APPLIED stays **—**.
Checked by · date Verifier · 2026-09-02 (revision 2)
### The five doors (front of the live card) Each door is **said / record / yes / —**: a sourced sentence or a fact. Never a second grade.
Door Measure said / record / yes / — sentence or fact URL date
Tax cap M66 **said** "Hold the line on property tax increases — stick to tax increases that residents and businesses can handle and find reasonable." No glide-path formula and no residential-rate cap. Named NO on the 7 May 2026 budget. The 9.34% residential figure is independently confirmed; the 35.52% cumulative figure is his campaign's own. [https://www.votestephenhammond.ca/priorities](https://www.votestephenhammond.ca/priorities) lastmod n/p, retrieved 2026-09-02
Downtown order M26 / M27 **said** "Support enforcement of existing bylaws to address street disorder." No Public Order Team and no 6am–10pm bylaw hours. Scored on M33, not on M26/M27. The 2024 daytime-sheltering motion is an M33 fact and is not imported under this door. [https://www.votestephenhammond.ca/priorities](https://www.votestephenhammond.ca/priorities) lastmod n/p, retrieved 2026-09-02
Housing M6 **said** "Victoria needs more homes, but housing policy has to work for the people who already live here." No unit target and no composition share. [https://www.votestephenhammond.ca/priorities](https://www.votestephenhammond.ca/priorities) lastmod n/p, retrieved 2026-09-02
Household bill M66d **—** Roads, water and sewer appear as core-infrastructure priorities, not as a combined household number. No utility line, no five-year trajectory. — —
Written program — **yes** Authorized 2026 site with three named commitments — a safer city, taxes people can afford, housing that works — each with a bullet list. Seven pages, financial agent named. No costings, no dates, no service standards, no lastmod. [https://www.votestephenhammond.ca/priorities](https://www.votestephenhammond.ca/priorities) lastmod n/p, retrieved 2026-09-02
--- ## The 12 topics Column key: **answer** = the mark · **quote or fact** = the verbatim sentence, then context · **URL** · **date** = lastmod, retrieved. Rules as written on . A dash is unknown, not a fail. No topic gets its own letter. ### 1 · Housing that gets built
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
1 M6 housing supply + composition **Partial 1.0** "Victoria needs more homes, but housing policy has to work for the people who already live here." · Commits to volume in the right places, with no unit target and no composition share. The only named instrument is "Review the Official Community Plan using updated population forecasts", which is not M6's target-and-composition instrument and is not comparable to it — a review can lower supply as easily as raise it. 📋 Record: NO on Missing Middle, 26 Jan 2023, passed 6–3, named against with Coleman and Gardiner; at the table he said "I think Councillor Caradonna is quite right that this is not a silver bullet that addresses affordability." Matches the 2026 "not anything and everything" / "right places" clause — not a miss, not in n. Context, not scored separately: he opposed the new OCP over renter displacement and process, not over zero new homes. [https://www.votestephenhammond.ca/priorities](https://www.votestephenhammond.ca/priorities) · [https://storeys.com/victoria-missing-middle-housing-initiative-passed-january-2023/](https://storeys.com/victoria-missing-middle-housing-initiative-passed-january-2023/) Plan retrieved 2026-09-02 · Record vote 26 Jan 2023 / press 27 Jan 2023
2 M6b land bank + co-ops — City land, a land bank and co-ops do not appear in the 2026 commitments. Gorge View Society board service is professional background, not a source. — —
3 M7 permits + AI pre-screening — No permit-time position, no service standard, nothing on AI pre-screening. Absence of a benchmark in term is Record, not Opposed. — —
4 M7b pattern-book housing — Pre-approved designs and an expedited stream do not appear. — —
5 M8/M8b 5% vacancy, DCC cuts, suite amnesty — No vacancy target, no DCC position, no suite amnesty. The 2023 Missing Middle NO is already carried on row 1 and is not re-marked here — one sentence, one measure. — —
### 2 · Downtown order
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
6 M26 Public Order Team — No unified command, co-location, or downtown operations desk. Visible police is scored on row 33. Bylaw enforcement is scored on row 10. — —
7 M26b civilian crisis response — "Continue to advocate for adequate mental health and addiction services that actually help people recover" is recovery-oriented health advocacy, not a civilian crisis-response capacity. Mention, so a dash. — —
8 M27 bylaw hours 6am–10pm — No bylaw-enforcement hours or staffing number anywhere in the 2026 programme. Enforcement without hours is scored on M33. — —
9 M28 data-targeted enforcement **📋 Record** "Unfortunately, this data shows what many Victoria residents, businesses, and visitors already know: a relatively small number of shelters and parks where people shelter create a disproportionate number of police calls for service." · He obtained VicPD call data by FOI and published it in Aug 2023: **19 shelter and encampment locations account for about 25% of all police calls**; 9,363 shelter-and-park calls in 2022; more than 29,000 over 2020–22; Rock Bay Landing alone 3,337 over three years. The Program's M28 rests on this finding. Shown, not scored: it is a 2023 action and there is no 2026 sentence on data-targeted enforcement, so it is not in n. **Discrepancy to reconcile in the Program, not on this card:** M28 states "about 24% of 2022 police calls from 19 addresses"; the published report says about **25% of all police calls** at 19 shelter and encampment **locations**, with 9,363 being the 2022 shelter-and-park subtotal. Fix the Program's wording before that figure is used in voter-facing material. [https://globalnews.ca/news/9891703/911-calls-for-encampments-victoria/](https://globalnews.ca/news/9891703/911-calls-for-encampments-victoria/) FOI reported 11 Aug 2023, retrieved 2026-09-02
10 M33 daytime sheltering bylaws **Close 2.0** "Support enforcement of existing bylaws to address street disorder." · Commits to enforcing existing bylaws, which is M33's whole instrument (enforce existing rules, no new rules, no new staff). Comparable, not Same: daytime sheltering is not named in the 2026 bullet and the parks 7 AM standard is not stated. 📋 Record: he moved the 18 Jul 2024 motion directing staff to cost and resource ending illegal daytime sheltering in all parks and boulevards, passed 8–1 with Kim alone opposed — matches, not a miss, not a second mark. Not capped: this cell is a hit. [https://www.votestephenhammond.ca/priorities](https://www.votestephenhammond.ca/priorities) · [https://victoriabuzz.com/2024/07/victoria-councillor-seeks-to-end-all-daytime-sheltering-in-parks-and-on-boulevards/](https://victoriabuzz.com/2024/07/victoria-councillor-seeks-to-end-all-daytime-sheltering-in-parks-and-on-boulevards/) Plan retrieved 2026-09-02 · Record 18 Jul 2024 / press 18 Jul 2024
11 M33b drug-use buffer (City: list + bylaw/DPOT + VicPD/CDSA; not City seizure) — Buffer zones do not appear on the 2026 priorities page. His Sept 2023 motion asked staff to draft a 30-metre ban around an expanded list of child-focused spaces; it was put on hold on the provincial pivot and never voted on the substance. Record of an unadopted file, not a 2026 Plan cell. Do not invent a mark from a postponed motion. The About page line "pushed for stronger limits on illicit drug use near child-focused spaces" is a 2026 restatement of that same postponed file, not a new commitment. — —
12 M34–M37 encampments, reclaiming spaces, night lighting — "Ensure parks and public spaces remain safe and accessible for all residents" raises parks without a removal protocol, a compliance window, named spaces, or night lighting. Mention, so a dash. The 2024 motion's encampment-harm clause sits inside the sentence already used on row 10. — —
### 3 · Household bill
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
13 M66 tax glide path (capped on the residential rate) **Partial+ 1.5** "Hold the line on property tax increases — stick to tax increases that residents and businesses can handle and find reasonable." · Commits to holding residential increases to what people can handle. Target, no instrument: no cap number, no year-path, no override rule, no ratio rule. 📋 Record: NO on the 7 May 2026 budget, one of three named opposed with Gardiner and Kim; the budget was 7.28% aggregate, 9.34% residential and 4.78% business. His stated reason is the opposite of Kim's — he opposed because the residential hike was too high. The vote is a hit, not a miss. Opposed −1.0 is the higher-tax treatment and is not applied. Not capped. [https://www.votestephenhammond.ca/priorities](https://www.votestephenhammond.ca/priorities) · [https://vicnews.com/2026/05/11/group-consensus-victoria-approves-7-28-tax-hike-with-3-members-opposed/](https://vicnews.com/2026/05/11/group-consensus-victoria-approves-7-28-tax-hike-with-3-members-opposed/) Plan retrieved 2026-09-02 · Record 7 May 2026 / press 11 May 2026
14 M66b/c over-collection refund + debt rule — "Ensure the City has sufficient reserves to look after the future without going into debt" mentions reserves and debt with no refund trigger, no 1.5% threshold, no debt ratio, no supermajority, no published debt set. Mention, so a dash. Protecting reserves is not M66b's over-collection refund. — —
15 M66d the Household Bill — "Prioritize core infrastructure: roads, water, sewer, parks and public safety" names the pieces, not a combined household number, and carries no utility-fee discipline and no five-year forward view. Mention, so a dash. — —
16 M70/M70b provincial downloading ledger — No downloading ledger, no refusal threshold, no twice-yearly UBCM/FCM resolutions. The 2024 Q&A framing that cities "can only do as much as the courts allow us to do" is pre-2026 and is a frame, not an instrument. — —
17 M70c CRD cost and the Goldstream plant — Regional Water Supply Commission appointment is a seat held, not a source. The plant, CRD rate trajectory and the rate-impact statement do not appear. — —
18 M71–M73d business, downtown, one mandate not a new office **Partial 1.0** "Work with businesses to address security concerns and restore confidence in downtown." · Commits to a downtown-business action. No vacancy target, no Team Victoria mandate, no Strategic Economic Plan, no Conference Centre numbers. Security cost-spreading is a different instrument and is carried on row 31, not scored from this sentence. [https://www.votestephenhammond.ca/priorities](https://www.votestephenhammond.ca/priorities) lastmod n/p, retrieved 2026-09-02
19 M74/M75/M76 capital threshold, short-stay parking (15-min grace; first-hour gated Year 2), permit fees — No 15-minute grace, no first-hour position, no \$25M capital-approval threshold, no small-renovation fee schedule. His 2024 remark that he disliked a parking-rate increase is pre-2026 and is not the M24/M75 instrument. — —
### 4 · Host Nations
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
20 M1–M5 Host Nations Foundation. Topic never drops out of the 12. A dash is still allowed on M1–M5. — No government-to-government table, procurement target, place-name programme, cultural protocol, or urban Indigenous liaison anywhere in the 2026 programme. The 21 May 2026 graffiti motion's consultation list naming Indigenous nations is a consultation instruction inside a different motion, not the Foundation, and is not a source here. Professional background is not a source. Targeted searching for a 2026 Hammond statement on the Host Nations returned nothing. — —
### 5 · Homelessness and waitlists
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
21 M9/M9b/M64 tenant protections, STR, indoor heat (M9c struck; 26°C gated) **Close 2.0** "When tenants are evicted for redevelopment, I want to ensure we give tenants proper compensation." · Commits, and has taken the action: on 30 Jul 2026 he moved the amendment that raised long-tenancy compensation above the staff recommendation — 5 months' rent at 5–9 years scaling to 24 months' rent at 40+ years, moving expenses to \$1,000–\$1,500 — and it carried unanimously. That is M9's named compensation instrument, delivered in the campaign year. Comparable, not Same: the cluster's other limbs are absent — no 12-month notice rule, no documented right of return, no replacement-unit ratio, no Renters' Hub commitment, no STR licensing (M9b), no indoor-heat standard (M64). M9c is struck and is not scored. His 2026 platform sentence carries the same commitment: "long-term tenants should receive much stronger compensation, because many will be forced to look for new homes at today's much higher market rents." TRAC board service is professional background, not a source. [https://www.castanetkamloops.net/news/BC/626637/Compensation-hiked-for-long-term-Victoria-tenants-displaced-by-development](https://www.castanetkamloops.net/news/BC/626637/Compensation-hiked-for-long-term-Victoria-tenants-displaced-by-development) · [https://www.votestephenhammond.ca/priorities](https://www.votestephenhammond.ca/priorities) Vote 30 Jul 2026 / press 31 Jul 2026 · Plan retrieved 2026-09-02
22 M10 transparent algorithmic waitlists — Waitlists, Coordinated Access, point-based scoring and queue transparency do not appear. — —
23 M11 Housing First + STEP throughput — No 50% unsheltered target, no Housing First named, no STEP throughput, no quarterly count, no fair-share ask of the other twelve municipalities. "We can support people who need help while also expecting clean, safe, functioning public spaces for everyone" (6 Jul 2026 launch) raises the goal without an instrument. Mention, so a dash. — —
### 6 · Families
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
24 M12/M13b/M13c childcare, doctors, youth (M13 school food is \$0 → M13d) — Childcare spaces, family-doctor recruitment and the 18–25 cohort do not appear. Big Brothers mentoring is volunteer background, not a source. — —
25 M13d standing School District 61 agreement — Schools and SD61 do not appear. M13 school food is \$0 and lives here only as M13d — nothing to score. — —
### 7 · Streets and mobility
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
26 M14/M16/M17/M18 cleanliness and the public realm **Partial 1.0** "For sure, we pay, the City of Victoria taxpayers pay close to \$500,000 a year." · Named mover of the 21 May 2026 motion directing staff to report on spray-paint retail restrictions to minors, secure or staff-access-only display, point-of-sale signage and retailer education, with exemptions, enforcement options, costs and consultation; carried, Caradonna and Dell opposed, Loughton absent. Commits to a graffiti instrument. Neither: retail restriction is a prevention lever and appears in none of M14 (48-hour removal standard), M16 (pests), M17 (sanitation hours) or M18 (murals). One sentence, this row: do not also mark Centennial Square or parks here. [https://vicnews.com/2026/05/22/victoria-looks-at-solutions-to-graffiti-problem-costing-nearly-500k/](https://vicnews.com/2026/05/22/victoria-looks-at-solutions-to-graffiti-problem-costing-nearly-500k/) Vote 21 May 2026 / press 22 May 2026, retrieved 2026-09-02
27 M19/M22/M38/M40–M42b mobility + Vision Zero (M39 30 km/h struck; calming is M38) — No adaptive-signal programme, no Vision Zero audit, no named corridor, no calming design, no speed-enforcement nomination list. M39 is struck — not scored. — —
28 M20b/M23b walking and transit the City controls — No sidewalk-gap inventory, no crossing standard, no City-controlled transit-lever list, no published annual transit position. — —
29 M24b/M25b accessibility and public washrooms — Public washrooms and an accessibility audit do not appear. Western Institute for the Deaf and Hard of Hearing board service is professional background, not a source. — —
30 M25 fix roads first — Roads appear in the core-infrastructure bullet already used to dash row 15. That list does not sequence maintenance ahead of new capital and carries no pothole standard. Mention, so a dash. One sentence, one measure. — —
### 8 · Policing and published safety
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
31 M28b business security cost-spreading **📋 Record** He moved the 6 Jul 2023 motion asking staff to examine costs and funding mechanisms to enhance security in areas hit by crime and by the effects of encampments and supportive-housing sites: "It's a great burden, a great expense, and my motion was just to spread that out, so that where you've got problems, the whole city as a whole will come and help with that security a little bit." Defeated. That is M28b's instrument, authored and moved by him — but it is a 2023 action with no 2026 sentence naming cost-spreading, so it is shown, not scored, and not in n. The 2026 "work with businesses to address security concerns" sentence is already scored on row 18 and cannot carry a second mark. A separate 4 Jul 2024 compensation-study motion failed 4–5 and is context, not a second Record line. [https://globalnews.ca/news/9815585/victoria-security-motion-defeated/](https://globalnews.ca/news/9815585/victoria-security-motion-defeated/) Motion 6 Jul 2023 / press 6 Jul 2023, retrieved 2026-09-02
32 M28d community paramedicine — Community paramedicine is not named. The 2024 Pandora paramedic assault is the stated occasion for the M33 motion, not an M28d position. — —
33 M29/M29b VicPD funding + regional review (convene-and-publish; no binding other force) **Partial 1.0** "Continue to support a visible police presence in Victoria's downtown." · Commits to police presence. Neither: not the Esquimalt funding-formula settlement with mediation, and not a convene-and-publish regional services review. 📋 Record: named against cutting new patrol officers from four to two, motion carried 5–4 on 3 Mar 2026, with Alto, Gardiner and Coleman also opposed to the cut. Matching, not in n. Gardiner's "defunding the police" line is hers and is not copied onto him; the named vote is the fact. [https://www.votestephenhammond.ca/priorities](https://www.votestephenhammond.ca/priorities) · [https://cheknews.ca/victoria-approves-2-not-4-officers-for-vicpd-slashes-reserve-contributions-1309089/](https://cheknews.ca/victoria-approves-2-not-4-officers-for-vicpd-slashes-reserve-contributions-1309089/) Plan retrieved 2026-09-02 · Record 3 Mar 2026
34 M30 smart LED lights, no surveillance — Streetlighting, LED conversion and the no-City-cameras limit do not appear. — —
35 M31/M31b/M31c/M32 safety dashboard, published enforcement record, crime target — No safety dashboard, no published enforcement record, no crime-reduction number, no performance-contract restatement of the CSWB plan. — —
### 9 · Beauty as a public good
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
36 M43–M46b heritage and cultural venues — Heritage design standards, street furniture and cultural-venue protection do not appear. Opposing Centennial Square changes is a fiscal-timing position on the About page, not a heritage-standards cell, and is not scored here. — —
37 M45b/c pedestrianisation and the signature project — No pedestrian-priority zone and no signature-project shortlist. Centennial Square opposition is not scored as disagreement with M45c: M45c is referendum-gated and cost-shared, which is not what he opposed. — —
38 M47–M49 heritage incentives, lighting, parks — Parks appear as safety and access on row 12 (dash) and as core infrastructure on row 15 (dash). No heritage-incentive fund, no ornamental-lighting hours, no parks restoration programme. The sequoia is inside the Centennial Square anecdote, not this cell. — —
39 M50/M50b/M51/M52 culture, sport, and the arts funding floor — "cultural events" sits inside the neighbourhood-associations sentence scored on row 53. One sentence, one measure. No arts funding floor, no extended civic hours, no sport instrument. The 10 Apr 2026 op-ed opposing a \$175K curling-club grant is a grant-scrutiny position and is noted as context on row 41, not as an arts or sport mark. — —
### 10 · A smaller scored Hall
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
40 M15 managed competition — Competitive testing of City services does not appear. Absence is Record, not Opposed. The ❌ on managed competition was already removed from the live profile for having no source — do not restore it. — —
41 M65 rotating zero-based reviews **Partial 1.0** "Conduct a thorough review of city spending to identify expenditures that aren't needed or can be phased-in over time." · Commits to a spending review. Neither: not zero-based, no rotating 3–4 service areas per cycle, no published three-part jurisdiction/outcomes/duplication test, no grants-over-\$50K review, no savings target. The 7 May budget NO is scored on row 13, not here. **Open source that could move this cell:** his 10 Apr 2026 Times Colonist op-ed "Victoria is wrong to give \$175K to curling club", listed on his own campaign news page, argues against a grant where a more accountable option existed — that is close to M65's grant test. The op-ed is behind a paywall and was not read this pass, so no upgrade was applied on unread text. [https://www.votestephenhammond.ca/priorities](https://www.votestephenhammond.ca/priorities) · unread: [https://www.timescolonist.com/opinion/comment-victoria-is-wrong-to-give-175k-to-curling-club-12117498](https://www.timescolonist.com/opinion/comment-victoria-is-wrong-to-give-175k-to-curling-club-12117498) Plan retrieved 2026-09-02 · op-ed 10 Apr 2026, unread
42 M67 quarterly performance dashboard — No KPI set, no cadence, no dashboard. Launch-day accountability language is a Mention with no instrument. — —
43 M68 overhead reduction by attrition — Headcount, attrition and administrative overhead do not appear. — —
44 M69 real-estate rationalisation — City real-estate holdings, the utilisation audit and disposition rules do not appear. — —
45 M53/M53b/M53c GIS, AI consultation imagery, LIDAR — GIS, consultation imagery and LIDAR do not appear. — —
46 M53d published municipal AI standard — Municipal use of AI does not appear. — —
47 M54–M57 local-tech procurement, open data, Wi-Fi, EV charging — Procurement preference, open data, public Wi-Fi and EV charging do not appear. — —
### 11 · Climate and trees as operations
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
48 M58/M58b/M64b climate, district energy, seismic — Climate Leadership Plan delivery, district energy and seismic resilience do not appear. The Missing Middle opponents' greenspace argument is the 2023 housing vote, already under row 1 as 📋, not a climate cell. — —
49 M59–M63 trees, mode share, ecosystems, emergency preparedness — No 5,000-tree target, no canopy number, no mode-share instrument, no stormwater sequencing, no emergency-preparedness position. The sequoia is Centennial Square context, not a trees programme. — —
### 12 · Neighbourhoods and integrity
# measure what it is answer quote or fact URL date
50 M77/M78/M78b \$25M referendum threshold, 5-step process, material-change rule — Opposing Centennial Square as poorly timed is not a \$25M threshold, a 5-step sequence, or a material-change rule. No referendum threshold is named anywhere in the 2026 programme. — —
51 M79/M79b Integrity Commissioner + 60-day consultation response — No Integrity Commissioner and no 60-day consultation-response or draft-back standard. This was downgraded from a tick in v1.8 because no statement naming an Integrity Commissioner was located, and none was located this pass either. Council-pay is scored on row 52, not here. — —
52 M79c–f lobbyist registry, FOI fee, remuneration **Partial+ 1.5** "He didn't object to a proper review of council compensation for future councils. However, he did object to sitting councillors voting themselves a large raise in the middle of their term, while residents were facing major tax increases." · 2026 campaign text, Commits to the next-term-only rule, which is M79f's instrument exactly ("any change to Council remuneration takes effect only at the start of the following term"). Marked Partial+ rather than Partial because the instrument match on that limb is verbatim, and rather than Close because three of the cluster's other instruments are wholly absent — no published mandate letters, no lobbyist registry, no FOI-fee waiver. 📋 Record context: named NO on the March 2024 immediate raise of about 25%, and at the time said "I still hold firm to my view that whatever recommendation this panel comes to any increases must be held over to the next council"; council later backed away. **FLAG for Joa:** the first pass marked this Partial 1.0. See fragility note. [https://www.votestephenhammond.ca/about](https://www.votestephenhammond.ca/about) · [https://goldstreamgazette.com/2024/04/05/victoria-council-pauses-pay-raise-strikes-task-force-for-advice/](https://goldstreamgazette.com/2024/04/05/victoria-council-pauses-pay-raise-strikes-task-force-for-advice/) About retrieved 2026-09-02 · Record vote 4 Apr 2024 / press 5 Apr 2024
53 M80/M80b/M80c neighbourhoods, language access, Local Area Plans **Partial 1.0** "Ensure there is sufficient funding for neighbourhood associations and cultural events that make living in Victoria enjoyable." · Commits to neighbourhood-association funding. Neither: no grant-line number, no plain-language or French standard, no two-plans-per-year Local Area Plan programme. Cultural events in the same bullet are not scored on row 39. "Allow residents to have a real say in their city" is the same neighbourhood-voice claim, not a second mark. The OCP review is housing-planning context on row 1, not an LAP programme. [https://www.votestephenhammond.ca/priorities](https://www.votestephenhammond.ca/priorities) lastmod n/p, retrieved 2026-09-02
54 M82/M82b community surveys, turnout and ballot access — Annual surveys, advance-vote days, voting places and turnout instruments do not appear. — —
55 M81 Saanich amalgamation (one line, not the whole topic) **📋 Record** Named NO on 25 Jun 2026 on the non-binding ballot question, carried 5–4, opposed with Caradonna, Gardiner and Thompson. Reported reason: he held that there should be a meaningful vote — that is, a binding referendum rather than an opinion question. Shown, not scored, because the report is a paraphrase and no verbatim 2026 sentence was located. **Do not recode this as Opposed.** M81's own endpoint is to return to the Province and request a binding referendum, so a NO cast in favour of a binding vote is not opposition to the measure; it sits with M81's direction while rejecting the instrument M81 assumes will proceed. [https://vicnews.com/2026/06/26/victoria-plans-to-pose-non-binding-amalgamation-opinion-question-at-the-polls/](https://vicnews.com/2026/06/26/victoria-plans-to-pose-non-binding-amalgamation-opinion-question-at-the-polls/) Vote 25 Jun 2026 / press 26 Jun 2026, retrieved 2026-09-02
